clue.text: Some ropy stuff that's found along the coast

definitions.meaning: a single thread or fibre twisted with others to make a rope
an old and poetic word for the shore or beach, as in London's street by the Thames

explanation.surface: A beachcomber picks up bits of frayed rope washed up by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings: a fibre of rope, and the shoreline (a sense kept in the name of the Strand, a London street that once ran along the Thames bank).
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: a twisted fibre in a rope, and a literary word for a beach.

clue.text: Deity with short name, an old character

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
N is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A god with a clipped name sounds like a quaint figure from history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' here means a written letter: the thorn was an Old English rune for the TH sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorn is a letter of the Old English alphabet, so it is literally an old written character.

clue.text: IT company shortly to introduce a nice new gadget

indicators.note: shortly says the company's name is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Apple is the computer and phone maker

indicators.note: new says the letters of a nice are rearranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A tech firm is about to launch a pleasant new device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon' but trims APPLE to APPL; 'new' rearranges A NICE into IANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device or piece of equipment, which is what a gadget is.

clue.text: Part of formal attire not in good condition

definitions.meaning: a false shirt front worn with evening dress
shaky or unsound, as in a weak heart; usually spelt without the E but the E form is accepted

explanation.surface: An item of evening wear has seen better days.
explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings: a detachable shirt front, and the informal British adjective for unreliable or poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: A dickey is a starched false shirt front for dress wear, and dickey also means weak or unsound.

clue.text: Things hanging down having power to exterminate insects

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
to end something is to wipe it out
ants are insects

explanation.surface: Something dangling with the power to kill bugs, like a fly strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendants are ornaments that hang, typically from a necklace or a ceiling.

clue.text: How attender with pint is out to have a wild celebration

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the words before it are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A party guest with a pint in hand has gone out on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is HOW ATTENDER plus PINT; 'with' only joins them, and 'is out' rearranges all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go out and celebrate in a lively, extravagant way.

clue.text: Square cut up in game

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word for cut is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to snip is to cut

explanation.surface: A square of something is chopped up during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' is not a shape here but a square number: nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepins is the old skittles game of knocking down nine pins with a ball.

clue.text: A new girl, as some would say, is a darling

parts.note: gel is how a plummy upper-class speaker says girl

explanation.surface: A new girl at school is a delight.
explanation.walkthrough: GEL is a dictionary spelling of the posh pronunciation of 'girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone an angel is calling them a sweetheart or a lovely person.

clue.text: What could be construed into gnarliest shapes

indicators.note: construed means interpreted another way, so the letters of the next word can be read in a new order

explanation.surface: Something might be twisted into the most knotted forms imaginable.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangles are three-sided figures, an example of geometric shapes.

clue.text: Legal procedure to pursue company member — it comes to the crunch?

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so the legal term comes after the other pieces

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
an action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A lawyer files suit against a firm's employee, and things reach a decisive moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'when it comes to the crunch': compaction is literally crunching things together.
explanation.definitionFit: Compaction is pressing material tightly together, which a cryptic reading calls being brought to the crunch.

clue.text: Good old-style politician, smooth-tongued

parts.note: a Lib is a Liberal, of the British party largely replaced by the Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: A decent politician of the old school with a silver tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Glib describes fluent but shallow talk, the speech of someone smooth-tongued.

clue.text: Oblique dishing of dirt — nice!

indicators.note: dishing here means spoiling or messing up, so the letters that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sly, roundabout way of spreading gossip, delivered with sarcasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dishing the dirt' means gossiping, but here 'dishing' wrecks DIRT and NICE into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblique and indirect are synonyms: both mean not straightforward or slanting.

clue.text: Come down by river in the country

indicators.note: by means beside, so the river sits next to the word for come down

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
to land is to come down from the air

explanation.surface: A traveller alights beside a river somewhere in the provinces.
explanation.definitionFit: Poland is a country in central Europe.

clue.text: Has a sleep, rolling over for a length of time

indicators.note: rolling over turns the word round so it is read backwards

parts.note: someone who has a sleep naps

explanation.surface: A sleeper turns over in bed for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is a stretch or period of time, as in attention span.

clue.text: Head gives general rule to those listening

indicators.note: listeners hear the word, so its sound counts rather than its spelling

parts.note: a principle is a fundamental rule or law

explanation.surface: A headteacher lays down the rules for the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal is the head of a school or college, a chief person.

clue.text: Notice worker with medieval weapon

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
a bill is a medieval pole weapon with a hooked blade

explanation.surface: A labourer armed with an old-fashioned weapon is spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbill is a printed notice or flyer handed out to people.

clue.text: Inner circle coming down on terror, lacking resistance in beastly contest

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece comes down on top of the second, so it is written above it

parts.note: the bull is the centre of a target

indicators.note: lacking says the symbol for resistance is taken out of the word for terror

parts.note: fright is terror
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A clique swoops down on a reign of terror without opposition, in a brutal clash.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking R out of FRIGHT leaves FIGHT, which goes under BULL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfight is a contest with a bull, so it is literally a fight involving a beast.

clue.text: Like some wild animals Matabele treated

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wildlife in Matabeleland, the region of Zimbabwe, receives medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: Some wild animals can be domesticated or trained, which is what tameable describes.

clue.text: Attractive nibble with balti I've prepared

indicators.note: prepared like a dish, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tasty snack accompanies the curry someone has cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: A balti is a type of curry popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Live bait is a living worm or fish used to lure a fish to bite, an attractive nibble for it.

clue.text: The ultimate plastic bottles

indicators.note: bottles here means holds in, so the word contains the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Plastic bottles as the last word in packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimate means final, the one at the end of a series.

clue.text: American show girl embracing any number in a place for sailors

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of the musical West Side Story
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A Broadway chorus girl hugs a crowd of sailors at the docks.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a harbour for yachts and small boats, a base for leisure sailors.

clue.text: An eight-day celebration — one goes from do to do

definitions.meaning: in the Church calendar, a festival observed for eight days including the feast day

definitions.text: one goes from do to do
definitions.meaning: in sol-fa, a run of notes spanning do up to the next do

explanation.surface: A week-long festival where a party animal hops from one do to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a party but is the sol-fa note.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dictionary senses: an eight-note musical interval and an eight-day church festival.

clue.text: Tea service set up after start of afternoon

indicators.note: after says the reversed service follows the first letter
start of picks the opening letter of the following word
in a down clue, set up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: Afternoon tea is served from a laid-out set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea service' reads as crockery, but 'Tea' is the definition and 'service' is Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a strong black tea from the Indian state of the same name.

clue.text: Seaside accommodation chore getting wife to run around

indicators.note: around says the word for run goes around the other piece

parts.note: to hare is to run fast
fag is British slang for a tiresome job

explanation.surface: A holiday let means housework, so the wife is left dashing about.
explanation.definitionFit: Wharfage is the berthing space provided at a wharf, accommodation for ships at the waterside.

clue.text: Making a horticultural insertion is hard work

definitions.meaning: a shoot set into another plant's stem to grow there

explanation.surface: Gardening by splicing plants together is laborious.
explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings; 'graft' for hard work is everyday British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A graft is a scion inserted into a rootstock, and graft also means toil.

clue.text: Animals from those parts to the west

indicators.note: to the west says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wildlife roaming in some region out west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' marks the letters inside THOSE PARTS; in an across clue, 'to the west' means read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Apes such as gorillas and chimpanzees are a group of animals.

clue.text: Bring him around in the morning in the city

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the letters are moved into a different order

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning hours

explanation.surface: Someone is told to fetch a man over before noon in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Birmingham is a major city in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Take food, including meat given special heat treatment

indicators.note: including means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to feed is to take food, as an animal does
lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: A diner eats a meal with meat that has been specially cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Flambéed food has spirit poured over and set alight, a dramatic cooking treatment.

clue.text: Wily characters represented in statue

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cunning figures are depicted in a sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute and wily both mean shrewd and clever at getting an advantage.
